bib.title: BEIT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers

question: Can BERT-style masked prediction be made to pretrain vision Transformers by predicting discrete visual tokens of masked patches?
hypothesis: Predicting discrete visual tokens (not raw pixels) of masked patches avoids wasting capacity on short-range, high-frequency detail and gives better pretraining.
contributions: A masked image modeling task to pretrain vision Transformers self-supervised, with a variational autoencoder explanation
Pretraining and fine-tuning on image classification and semantic segmentation
Self-attention of BEIT separates semantic regions and object boundaries without annotation

method.summary: A ViT is pretrained by masking about 40% of 16x16 patches (blockwise) and predicting the dVAE (DALL-E) visual token of each masked patch with a softmax over 8192 codes. The pretrained encoder is then fine-tuned end to end for classification and ADE20K segmentation.
method.task: self-supervised masked image modeling pretraining; ImageNet classification and ADE20K segmentation fine-tuning

datasets.name: ImageNet-1K
datasets.size: about 1.2M images (text elsewhere says 1.3M); no labels used
datasets.preprocessing: random resized cropping, horizontal flipping, color jittering 0.4; 224x224

datasets.name: ImageNet-22K
datasets.split: 150 epochs self-supervised then 90 epochs intermediate fine-tuning (Appendix B)

models.name: BEIT-B
models.architecture: ViT-Base, learnable 1D position embeddings, [S] token, FFN 3072
models.init_from: random in [-0.02,0.02], output matrices of layer l rescaled by 1/sqrt(2l)
models.context: inferred: 14x14 patch grid plus [S] token at 224

models.name: BEIT-L
models.context: inferred: 14x14 patch grid plus [S] token at 224

models.name: BEIT+
models.architecture: BEIT with LayerScale and relative position bias (Appendix A)

training.objective: maximize log-likelihood of correct visual tokens at masked positions (Eq. 1); about 40% (at most 75 patches) patches masked by blockwise masking, min block 16 patches
training.optimizer: Adam, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, eps 1e-8 (cited as Loshchilov and Hutter, decoupled weight decay)
training.regularisation: stochastic depth 0.1; gradient clipping 3.0 base, 1.0 large

other.finetune_imagenet: Table 13: peak lr {2e-3,3e-3,4e-3,5e-3}, 100 epochs base/50 large, batch 1024, warmup 20/5, layer-wise lr decay 0.65 base/0.75 large, weight decay 0.05, label smoothing 0.1, stoch depth 0.1, RandAug 9/0.5, mixup 0.8, cutmix 1.0, erasing 0.25, min lr 1e-6, cosine; 384 res: 10 more epochs
other.finetune_cifar100: 150 epochs, batch 512, warmup 20, layer decay 0.65, weight decay 0.3
other.finetune_ade20k: Table 14: lr 1e-3, 160K steps, batch 16, layer decay 0.65, linear schedule, warmup 1500 steps, 512x512, stoch depth 0.1, wd 0.05, SETR-PUP task layer
other.linear_probe: AdamW 50 epochs lr 4e-3 cosine, batch 1024, wd 1e-4

inference.samples: single run per number; no seeds stated

metrics.name: top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: ImageNet-1K / CIFAR-100 classification accuracy after fine-tuning (avg-pooled patch features, linear softmax)

metrics.name: mIoU
metrics.definition: mean intersection over union averaged over 150 ADE20K categories, single-scale unless noted

metrics.name: reconstruction error
metrics.definition: mean absolute error of normalized RGB values

eval.protocol: single runs; no seeds or error bars reported

availability.data: ImageNet, ADE20K, CIFAR-100 public; in-house 70M not public

evidence.quote: The pre-training runs for about 500k steps (i.e., 800 epochs) with 2k batch size.

limits: Ablations use 300 epochs only and single runs; no seeds or error bars
Linear-probe quality is weak for base size (56.7) versus discriminative methods
Depends on a pretrained external DALL-E tokenizer
Only classification and segmentation tested; scaling to 1B-10B models is suggested, not shown
Large results use an unreleased in-house 70M labeled set
Table 4 ADE20K task layer unstated; Table 4 BEIT 300ep ADE20K 44.65 vs Table 5 ViT row 44.86 (UperNet)

terms.definition: randomly mask some percentage of image patches, then predict the visual tokens that correspond to the masked patches

code.snippet: Blockwise masking: repeat s<-Rand(16, 0.4N-|M|); r<-Rand(0.3,1/0.3); a<-sqrt(s*r); b<-sqrt(s/r); t<-Rand(0,h-a); l<-Rand(0,w-b); M<-M U {(i,j): i in [t,t+a), j in [l,l+b)} until |M|>0.4N
